- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 169): **A claim should be published with its refutation in the output space, not with its confidence in the metadata — and this is the first entry in the folder where a failed explanation is a deliverable rather than a result.** Every prior certificate here answers "how strong is the guarantee I have"; this one answers "here is the proposition, and here is the input on which it is false", returning the triple proven / refuted-with-witness / unknown. The demonstration is as cheap as it is decisive: the quote circuit agrees with the surrogate on 100% of the fitting dataset *and* on 100% of the bounded abstract domain, and the solver still produces a three-token input where the program and the model disagree — so agreement level carries no information about the existence of a counterexample, which is exactly the distinction this folder's pooled scores smooth away. For us the adoption is a reporting format, not a method: every prediction our white-box model emits should name its domain, its projection, its ablation semantics and the property asserted, and be reported as proven / refuted-with-witness / out-of-domain, because a predictor that can only say "usually right" is not making a claim anyone can check. (arxiv-2605.24033, arxiv-2602.16823, arxiv-2609.35686)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 169): **You can buy verifiability with architecture, and the paper prints the price — +0.196 OpenWebText loss and +9.12 WikiText-103 perplexity for the full SMT-friendly stack, with the normalization swap carrying almost all of it, and the author's own comparison says removing LayerNorm from pretrained weights currently beats replacing it in training.** This is the folder's cost-metric lesson at the level of the model rather than the read-out: the interpretable-by-design entry cost nothing in loss because it was scored on its own scale (a small model, a small task), whereas here the same bet is priced at GPT-2-small scale and loses visibly. The transferable habit is to state the interpretability tax *and* the alternative you were priced against — here trained-replacement versus post-hoc removal — since the honest reading is not "verifiability is expensive" but "verifiability is currently cheaper to obtain after training than during it". Read with the prototype-LM entry, the general rule for us is that any design-time change we recommend reports its loss delta at a scale where the baseline is strong, because a stack that trains stably is not the same claim as a stack that trains competitively. (arxiv-2605.24033, arxiv-2607.00510, arxiv-2605.11161)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 169): **A guarantee that passes through a surrogate should be published as a chain of named links, and the paper's own honest move is to say which link is the weak one — circuit fidelity to the model, surrogate fidelity to the circuit, program equivalence to the surrogate, with the symbol, the projection and the domain held fixed across all three.** This is the folder's two-denominator rule extended to three, and it differs from an averaged score in a way that matters practically: the middle link's strength is set by whether its validation was exhaustive over the domain or sampled, so the same top-line "verified" can mean two very different things and the entry can be compared with others only if that is stated. The same defect appears in this folder's judge pipeline (a description validated against a surrogate judge), in its paraphrased-input evaluations (a read-out validated against one rewrite model), and in its attribution proxies (an effect estimate validated against a first-order expansion), so the requirement generalises beyond verification: whenever our predictor's claim is checked through an intermediate object, the intermediate gets its own fidelity number and its own control. (arxiv-2605.24033, arxiv-2606.09899, arxiv-2506.02945)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 168): **A linear read-out over a frozen representation is not competing with the generative model that produced it — it is competing with that model's *own report*, and this is the first entry in the folder that scores a probe against that baseline rather than against chance.** Every read-out we hold is validated against a random or shuffled or orthogonal control; here the comparator is the judge's own numeric score, embedded into the model as a bias term so that the empty solution reproduces it exactly (`θ = 0 ⊕ 1, c = 0`), which turns "our probe works" into "our probe beats the model's introspection at a cost the model cannot match" — 4,096 parameters instead of billions, 0.775 GPU-minutes instead of 14.16 on the same data. That is the strongest form of the folder's recurring dominated-baseline argument, and it is what a *predictive* white-box model actually needs to show: not that a direction encodes the quantity, but that reading it is cheaper and more accurate than asking. The anchor construction is the cheap part worth stealing outright — every predictor we fit on top of an existing scorer should be parametrised so the zero-weight solution is that scorer, which makes the reported delta a delta and makes "never worse than the baseline" true by construction rather than by luck. (arxiv-2506.02945, arxiv-2605.11161, goodfire-com-research-reasoning-theater)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 168): **Fitting the level of a quantity and fitting its order are separate jobs, and optimising the first demonstrably destroys the second on the same rows — MSE halved while Kendall τ fell 0.272 → 0.214, and the fine-tuned baseline that nobody claimed was calibrated scores *better* on all three correlations.** This is the folder's two-denominator rule in its most mechanical form, because the two numbers are computed from one fitted model on one test set with no selection or filtering between them: the improvement is real on the metric the loss names, and the regression is real on the metric users of a ranker care about. The practical import is a reporting requirement, not a modelling one — any claim that our predictor "matches" a target publishes the fit statistic and the ranking statistic side by side, and says which one the loss optimised — and the companion observation is that accuracy and correlation do not co-move among the four judges here either (the multinomial judge wins exact accuracy on both rating datasets while losing Pearson r on the second), so a single headline number would have hidden the entire structure of the result. (arxiv-2506.02945, arxiv-2609.15533, arxiv-2603.01437)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 168): **The strongest arm is the one where the cheap method loses, and here the authors print it — with abundant labels the fine-tuned judge wins outright on the largest preference dataset, and the read-out's advantage is confined to the small-label regime their ablations actually show.** The claim being defended is statistical efficiency, and the paper defends it the way the folder's better entries do: by naming the condition under which the advantage is a *parameter-count* fact (4,096 versus billions) and showing the crossover rather than averaging over it, with SFT ahead at all training sizes under Prometheus on accuracy and ahead up to 20% of data only for the other base judge. Read against this folder's cost-metric and matched-budget entries, the rule generalises to a one-line pre-flight for any "cheaper model is competitive" claim of ours: state the regime where the expensive arm wins, and if there is none, suspect the budget was never matched. (arxiv-2506.02945, arxiv-2605.01555, arxiv-2602.16823)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 167): **The neighbourhood, not the input, is the correct unit for a read-out — and this is the first entry in the folder whose whole point is to score a dictionary over a *set* of reachable inputs rather than over the inputs that were sampled.** Every stability result the folder holds moves the *data* at fixed inputs (bootstrap resamples, seeds, paraphrase sets scored on average); this moves the *input* and asks whether the read-out survives anywhere in a region built from the model's own forward pass, which is the difference between "our features are usually there" and "no paraphrase in this hull can evict them". The numbers show the distinction is not academic: worst-layer top-20 overlap of 0.27 under a single WordNet synonym and 0.05 under an LLM rewrite, and a targeted point that removes all four safety-relevant features from the top-8 while the model is untouched. For us the adoption is direct and cheap — any prediction our white-box model makes about a component should carry the input set over which it is claimed, produced by propagating the model itself rather than by hand — and it reframes the folder's attack results: an adversarial example against an *interpretation* is not a robustness curiosity, it is the natural test of a predictor's domain. (arxiv-2609.15533, arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2606.06267)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 167): **A certificate can be independently loose and independently corrosive — verification-aware training tightened the verified bound ~90% and reported only 2–3 of the top 20 features as provably retained, so the honest headline is the pair, not the 90%.** This is the folder's two-denominator rule arriving at its sharpest form: the quantity that improved (the declared faithfulness gap) and the quantity that did not (preservation of the features the interpretation is actually made of) are computed from the same intervals, and the paper does say so — which is exactly why a reader who takes only the improved number will overstate the result. Two transferable habits follow. First, always publish the bracket: a witnessed lower bound and a certified upper bound on the same quantity, because their gap measures the verifier and the middle measures the claim, and a single "certified δ < X" hides both. Second, notice the non-monotonicity the ablation found — at ε = 0.01 both retrained stand-ins are *worse* in median δ than the untrained baseline (30.2 / 30.4 against 11.0), reversing only from ε = 0.05 — because a method that improves the metric at the operating point but degrades it at the smallest neighbourhood is a method whose gain is a regularity compromise, and the same signature appears in this folder's selection-filtered p-values and its matched-budget ablations. (arxiv-2609.15533, arxiv-2608.24037, arxiv-2605.06076)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 167): **The certificate nobody ran is one training run away, and its absence is the standard failure mode of a formalisation paper: without a stand-in fitted to a randomly initialised model, "we certified faithfulness" is indistinguishable from "we certified closeness to the thing we regressed onto".** The paper is unusually careful about the *other* confound — it explicitly refuses to treat a high Jaccard as sufficient, because a stand-in with large biases would keep the same safe features active regardless of input — but the same argument applies one level up and is not made: an SAE fitted to a random network could be δ-equivalent to that random block and show stability under paraphrase, so the certificate would be true and the interpretation empty. The folder already has the empirical half of this (`core/` evidence that auto-interpretation scores do not separate trained from random transformers) and the methodological half from the untrained-weight controls that flattened a linear-layer claim and a recurrence claim, so the synthetic arm now has three precedents and no excuse. Practical rule for us: every certification of our predictor carries an animal-control arm — the identical pipeline fitted to a model where the mechanism cannot exist — because that is the only way to separate machinery quality from structural fact. (arxiv-2609.15533, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2604.11791)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 166): **A "cleaner labels reveal the signal" argument is a selection experiment in disguise, and the missing arm is always the stratum that was thrown away — this paper is the clearest case in the folder because it never scores the responses the judges disagreed about.** Re-running the same test on the unanimous subset takes Gemma's honest strategy from p = 0.555/0.310 to 0.048/0.048 with d = 1.24 and calls the strengthening a validation of the signal, but the same arithmetic also turns a 100-prompt dataset into 63 responses with 60 of them in one class, and the disagreement stratum — where a *successful* monitor should be doing its hardest work — is dropped rather than reported. Read against the folder's other selection lessons (a pooled agreement rate computed on the prompts the model already gets right, an effect size compared against a copy effect measured elsewhere, an ablation run at a different scale from the main experiment), the rule generalises: whenever a claim is strengthened by filtering the evaluation set, the discarded part is a free and mandatory second report, and if the effect is absent there the finding is about the filter. Two cheap companions: publish the class ratio of the surviving groups next to every p-value, and state whether the filter is applied before or after the balance of groups is checked. (arxiv-2608.24037, arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2510.00845)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 166): **The trajectory, not the state, is the object most of this folder's read-outs implicitly assume — and the price of reading it is refusing one normalisation.** Every probe, patching and lens result here scores a residual vector at one site; this paper asks the same models for the *path* length and bending, which requires (i) sampling after attention and after MLP separately rather than at layer boundaries, and (ii) reconstructing the unnormalised stream, because LayerNorm rescales and re-centres each step and destroys exactly the magnitude information a path integral depends on. That second point is the transferable one and it is not free: any geometric or distance-based statistic we compute on post-LayerNorm activations — cosine between directions, decoder cosine against a dictionary, an interference matrix — is measured in a space whose radial coordinate has been normalised away, which is why this folder's cosine-based claims keep needing a *functional* control beside them. The companion warning is the composite: A′ sums salience and curvature at a fixed γ = 1 with no component ablation, so the paper cannot say which half carries the separation, and that is the same defect as a seven-metric battery whose judge and activation metrics disagree and a cost metric that manufactures a winner. (arxiv-2608.24037, arxiv-2606.12138, arxiv-2608.03913)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 164): **The natural-language branch of this field has converged on the same test this folder keeps arriving at from the circuit side — describe the thing as a classifier over its own exemplars and score it like one — and it is the cheapest instrument we do not yet own.** A hypothesis is scored by whether a reader holding only that sentence could sort 12 activating prompts from 12 matched controls; that is Detection F1, no ground truth needed, and it converts "is this description right?" into an ordinary supervised number. It is the description-side twin of the induce-and-repair certificate, of the matched-negative arm that flattens a localisation claim, and of the same-size-random-object control for a surrogate: in all four cases the claim is graded against *its own matched alternative* rather than against a nicer-looking version of itself. For a predictive white-box model the adoption is direct and cheap — our prediction is a claim about which prompts will behave a certain way, so the adjudication set is 12 and 12, and it costs one classifier call. (arxiv-2605.01555, arxiv-2602.00767, arxiv-2605.06076)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 164): **A seven-metric battery does not average away the disagreement between its metrics, and the disagreement is structured: activation-statistics metrics separate rival explanations cleanly while language-side metrics do not, so an LLM judge is a preference measure and never evidence.** In this paper's polysemantic case study the highest Surprisal AUROC and second-highest judge score belong to a hypothesis with p = 0.064 and d = 0.99, while the statistically dominant hypothesis scores mid on the judge; in its monosemantic case study the refined hypothesis has Detection F1 1.00 against 0.89 and d = 2.53 against 0.00 yet scores *lower* judge coherence (0.40 vs 0.00 is the one place it wins, but embedding similarity is 0.59 vs 0.52 and Surprisal 0.71 vs 0.77 — the language metrics are near-ties while the activation metrics are total). This is the same lesson the folder drew from an agreement rate computed only on prompts the model already gets right, and from borrowed figure-number checks: when metrics disagree, the ones grounded in a counterfactual are the ones to keep. Two practical consequences for us: never report a judge score as the headline for a read-out, and when two metrics conflict, report the conflict rather than the average — average ordinal rank is precisely the operation that hides it. (arxiv-2605.01555, arxiv-2605.11161, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 164): **A discovery method can win every baseline it is compared against and still be near-useless in absolute terms, and the tell is a metric the paper reports but does not headline — here ARI 0.315 against K-Means's 0.118 reads as a 2.7× win until you notice silhouette is 0.005, i.e. worse than the baseline it beats, and that the ablation variant collapses to ARI ≈0.03.** The structure being discovered is *local* (kNN neighbourhoods are informative) but *not globally segregated* (no separated clusters), which is exactly the geometry the folder's superposition and featurizer entries describe, and it means "we recover concept X by clustering" is a weaker claim than the comparison-to-baselines framing suggests. Two habits follow: always report an absolute-quality number alongside the relative win, and check whether the ablation and the main experiment are on the same scale before reading either — this paper's own note that 0.03 vs 0.315 comes from 200-vs-500 prompts and 17-vs-20 languages is the kind of disclosure that makes the main result vulnerable rather than safe. (arxiv-2605.01555, arxiv-2605.06076, arxiv-2608.03913)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 163): **Every faithfulness number in this folder is graded inside interpretability, and this paper is the field's own statement that the missing criterion is outside it — the concrete instrument is a comparative-utility baseline, not a better explanation metric.** A measured action has to beat prompting or a small adapter on the same task metric, and no entry in 160 has done that: our circuit, probe and steering evidence is benchmarked against random directions, shuffled labels and other interpretability methods, which is the "grading on a curve" the authors name and the same defect as the matched-random arm that flattens a localisation result, the linear-map R² a random-init model also reaches, and the pooled agreement rate computed on the prompts the model already gets right. For a predictive white-box model the translation is direct and cheap: our predictor's output is a *routing or editing decision*, and its null is not a shuffled predictor but the decision a practitioner would make without internals — ask whether the prediction changes any action, then whether that action beats the no-internals alternative. (arxiv-2605.11161, arxiv-2605.06076, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 163): **The folder's two-sided intervention discipline now has a published name and a semantic-task form: faithfulness is flipping the target computation while verifying an unrelated behaviour is intact — and the second half is the half every entry here omits.** Specificity is scored twice, "does this component beat its alternatives" and "does intervening leave unrelated benchmarks unchanged", and the second is exactly the collateral-damage check that steering, ablation and editing results in this folder rarely report. Read against the induce-and-repair certificate (a direction must create the behaviour and remove it), the write-site ablation (same contrast, two injection points, 64 points apart) and the disentanglement criterion from the SDT papers, the complete report for any intervention is now four cells: target-behaviour change under the intervention, target-behaviour change under a matched control, unrelated-behaviour change under the intervention, and the size at which parseability collapses. (arxiv-2605.11161, arxiv-2602.00767, arxiv-2605.10664)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 163): **A criterion with two independent axes invites a scoring error, and this framework has it: concreteness and validation are declared orthogonal, yet every validated exemplar in it is a case where the insight and the intervention were the same act — so the framework scores tooling well and prediction badly.** An editing method that is conceived, built and measured is one artifact; a description that predicts what will happen under an intervention is two, and its validation cost lives in the gap between them. The honest adaptation for us is to keep their axes and add a third coordinate the paper does not need: *distance between claim and action*, i.e. how many unverified inferential steps separate what we assert from what we measure. That number is precisely where the folder's illusion literature lives — a direction whose effect is large where the copy effect is zero, a surrogate that beats random edges only past 80% of the network, an attribution patching estimate with 750% error after local correction — and it is a coordinate a reader can check, unlike a general impression of rigor. (arxiv-2605.11161, arxiv-2611.05033, arxiv-2606.09899)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 162): **A description of a network is a map of one instant, and the first measured cost of that in this folder is an accuracy gain that survives replacing the map with a random one — mechanical localisation of 800 components beat full fine-tuning and was indistinguishable from freezing 800 arbitrary components, while producing *more* circuit movement than not freezing anything at all.** The transferable instrument is the matched-random arm at the same budget and the same attention/MLP ratio, which is the control every "our localisation helps" claim owes and almost none run; and the diagnostic that explains the flattening is the circuit-scale sweep, where the method only separates from random at ~80% of the network, i.e. exactly where its compactness claim dies. Read against the folder's other cost-metric lesson (compactness is a claim about connectivity, not unit count) and its coverage-versus-compactness pairs, the rule for us is blunt: a predictive white-box model is only worth its size where it beats a same-size random object, and the size at which it does is a published number, not a design preference. (arxiv-2605.06076, arxiv-2608.03913, arxiv-2606.06267)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 162): **Stability has been used in this folder as a property of the *method* (do two resamples agree), and this paper shows it is also a property of the *checkpoint* — a mechanism is either consolidated enough to be sampled consistently at all, or it is still moving, and the two readings are separable because one is measured across data subsets at fixed weights and the other across weights.** The expected rank correlation between circuits from two independent 20% halves rises with dataset size and with initial mastery while circuit distance stays flat under those same manipulations, which gives a clean 2×2: moving-but-pinned-down ("migrating intact knowledge"), still-here-but-loose ("refining in place"), and the pathological corner where localisation results behave like random ones. For a predictive model this reframes what a training-level eval should report — not "does the read-out survive retraining" but distance and stability *as a pair through the run*, because the entry's own undoing was that its success stories were the tasks where distance happened to be small. (arxiv-2605.06076, arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2606.06267)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 162): **Where a mechanism sits predicts how quickly it goes stale, and this is the folder's first entry to make component type a temporal variable — attention circuits (skills) migrated roughly twice as far as MLP circuits (facts) under the same optimisation, so any interpretability result quoted from a mid-training checkpoint carries a shelf life set by where in the network it was measured.** That is the training-axis twin of the recurrence entry's point that depth is not a single axis, and it lands on us directly: the folder's circuit, probe and steering results are overwhelmingly attention-side and are quoted at a fixed checkpoint, so they inherit the shorter shelf life, while the MLP-side dictionary and knowledge-editing results inherit the longer one — which is also why the applied literature's successes cluster on factual editing. The practical addition to our reporting is one column: the expected movement of the unit class the claim is about, measured on the same model by the cheapest available proxy (causal-effect drift over a few checkpoints), because a prediction that is right today and wrong after the next fine-tuning stage is a different deliverable from one that is right about the finished model. (arxiv-2605.06076, arxiv-2604.11791, arxiv-2608.03913)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 161): **The estimand can be designed into the architecture, and this is the first entry in the folder that pays the full price for it — a scaling run plus a curvature theorem rather than a demo.** Every other attribution entry we hold estimates influence post hoc over dense parameters and then argues about approximation quality; PRISM instead trains the prediction to be a sparse non-negative mixture over units that clustering keeps near real activations, so "which training examples" becomes a cached sparse retrieval. The transferable part is the symmetric clustering pair (each unit pulled to its nearest example, each example pulled to its nearest unit) — the R1-only ablation reaching 0.473 coverage against 0.987 for the symmetric objective is the evidence that the two directions are not interchangeable.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 161): an interpretable channel can be readable and non-load-bearing at once, and PRISM ships the two numbers that decide it — residual share, and the CE increase from removing the prototypes versus removing the residual. The folder has met this before in feature-ablation leverage and in off-target steering, but never with the load-bearing claim stated as a matched pair of ablations on the same rows. Our own read-outs should report both directions, because "the prototypes carry most of the computation" is only true where the residual is small, and that is a property of the distribution, not of the architecture.
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 161): **A speedup claim is only as good as the arm that isolates its cause — here the prototype-subspace restriction gave ~2× and the boring caching of sparse records gave the 470×.** Three arms in one ladder (no curvature, diagonal stiffness, full CG solve) against a dense reference plus a matched-storage control is the reporting shape worth copying, and it is exactly the discipline the folder's cost-metric entry asked for. Open flag: κ falling from 6.18e7 to 4.56e2 as a function of one loss coefficient needs a matched uniform-ridge arm before it is read as geometry rather than as regularisation strength — the paper calls it structured ridge but never runs the ridge control.

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 151): **A probe earns the word "representation" only against a norm-matched orthogonal perturbation, and this is the cleanest version of that control in the folder because it also states its own saturation point.** Every steering claim the folder has recorded compares a direction against a random or shuffled or Gaussian vector; this paper compares against a direction drawn orthogonal to the probe *and rescales it to the same norm per example*, which holds magnitude fixed and varies only semantic content — the same discipline the SWD entry's random-orthogonal factorization applied to decomposition and the non-identifiability entry applied at the logit level. The extra move worth copying is the honest ceiling: on a balanced binary task, general reasoning collapse should converge on 50% flips, and the orthogonal curves here do saturate near 0.5, so the interesting quantity is the *gap to saturation*, not the gap to zero. That reframes what a direction claim needs: a norm-matched orthogonal arm, a stated degradation ceiling, and a parse-failure ledger, since at large dose the model stops producing parseable answers at all. (arxiv-2603.01437, arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2608.03913)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 151): **Where an intervention acts and what a direction means are separable, and this paper's own open question is the folder's recurring confound in a new costume — the intervention covered the answer tokens as well as the reasoning tokens, so the effect could be direct answer-token biasing rather than propagation from a pre-reasoning belief, and their remark that 	his concerns where the intervention exerts its influence, rather than what the direction represents" is exactly the distinction a predictive white-box model must keep.** Read against the write-site ablation (same contrast at attention vs MLP output differing by 64 points) and the KV-cache compounding result (a constant dose becomes a growing cumulative perturbation across turns), the general requirement is explicit: every intervention result of ours publishes its *plane* — which positions, which layers, whether the answer region is inside the intervention — because a predictor scored against an unstated plane is being asked to extrapolate across a variable nobody measured. The compensating evidence here is the trace typology: coherent, conclusion-aligned confabulation is hard to explain by generic collapse, and correct-premise non-entailment is hard to explain by a reasoning-mediated pathway, so the *content* of the induced failure localises the mechanism when the geometry of the intervention cannot. (arxiv-2603.01437, arxiv-2605.10664, arxiv-2608.03913)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 151): **Read-out strength and CoT usefulness anticorrelate across tasks, which gives us a routing rule rather than a single number — the probe is strong exactly where the written reasoning is decorative (Social Chemistry 0.988–1.000 AUC, where CoT adds almost nothing) and collapses where the reasoning is doing the work (Logical Deduction 0.688–0.878, the only task where removing CoT destroys accuracy and where a reasoning-trained model shows no pre-reasoning signal at all).** The transferable habit is to report, per task, both the activation-side predictive score and a text-side sufficiency estimate (here: accuracy with and without the rationale), because their ratio says which instrument is appropriate; a weak probe on a task where the rationale is load-bearing is not a failed probe but a correct statement that the computation happens in text. This is the same shape as the folder's other two-denominator lessons — reconstruction error beside firing coverage, faithfulness beside stability — and it is the argument for treating the CoT and the residual stream as two measurement channels whose *divergence* is the finding, rather than as competing explanations where the better number wins. (arxiv-2603.01437, goodfire-com-research-reasoning-theater, arxiv-2509.13316)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 152): **A denominator fitted to one canonical output per input cannot see its own blind spot, and this paper puts exact arithmetic on the loss — the trace-channel twin of every probe control in this folder.** If SFT reveals only a subset of valid traces per prompt, the true law and an alternative that treats the visible subset as the whole conditional produce identical supervised observations, and their L1 distance is exactly twice the expected hidden mass; the missing local events are therefore unidentifiable rather than under-sampled, and no amount of data repairs it (Appendix D, Theorem D.1). That converts a family of things this folder does in single-sample form — one generation per prompt for a decoder, one contrast set per direction, one ablation convention per circuit, one seed per claim — into claims with a nameable defect: the instrument is being scored on a region of the distribution it never observed, and the fact that nothing contradicts it is a property of the censoring, not of the model. The practical requirement is a support statement with every read-out: which outputs were visible to the fitting procedure, what mass was left out, and which of the paper's claims depend on the excluded part. The compensating half is the RL enrichment proposition, which is the folder's known-positive control in theorem form — a hidden event becomes identifiable only if the policy can reach it and the verifier prefers traces containing it — and that is a serviceable checklist for whether an experiment of ours could in principle have learned a distinction it claims to have learned. (arxiv-2606.18089, arxiv-2509.13316, arxiv-2602.06801)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 152): **Out-of-distribution should be defined on the combination of factors, not on the input surface, and this is the sharpest version of that test in the folder — every held-out instance's atoms appear elsewhere in training, so only the recombination is new.** The composition signature makes the criterion mechanical: a test trace whose skill sequence and routing pattern were never jointly seen is OOD even though each step was; and the numbers show the criterion has teeth, with SFT collapsing on unseen compositions (0.30 → 0.22 for depth 2 → 3) while RL holds them, and RL on compounds beating RL on atoms by 27.8 points at matched checkpoint and budget. For a predictive white-box model this is the eval shape to import wholesale, because the cheap alternative — hold out inputs — is passed by any method that stores templates, and the folder's circuit, probe and steering evaluations mostly hold out inputs. The companion result is that composability must be *exercised* rather than merely present: withholding a skill and re-injecting it in isolation recovers far less than re-injecting it inside compositions, and the identical isolated re-injection placed in the SFT stage instead of the RL stage does almost nothing — so for us, a component interface we claim to understand should be scored on configurations where it meets a new neighbour, and one that was only ever observed in its usual context should be marked unexercised rather than understood. (arxiv-2606.18089, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, arxiv-2603.01437)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 149): **A description should be graded on the ranking it gives to the true cause among matched alternatives, and this is the first number in the folder on that scale — 0.457 down to 0.381 when one hop of downstream context is added, while the descriptor the field quotes most, the feature's top unembeds, moved the ranking by almost nothing.** Two things follow immediately. The evaluation design is buildable for us at no annotation cost: construct groups whose local descriptors are equal by construction, hold the ground truth in the intervention that defines the group, and score any read-out (probe, dictionary label, node summary) by the position-balanced normalised rank it assigns the known cause — which grades exactly the artefact a predictive white-box model emits, and needs no faithfulness machinery. And the downgrade rule: a component summary consisting of firing examples plus direct logit preferences is effectively *unranked* against causally distinct alternatives, because both were shown to produce near-identical descriptors on features that steering separates cleanly. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-headvis-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 149): **The output of a mechanistic hypothesis is usually a discriminating input, not a label — and both case studies are the same cheap move.** *Green-the-hex-number* versus *green-the-colour-word* became decidable only when the authors built a prompt where the two readings predict different steering outcomes, and *describing a willingness to act* versus *acting on it* became decidable only because the audit scenario had a behaviour separating them. Set next to the folder's headvis lesson (a description's failure mode is a missing qualifier, not a wrong label), this is the constructive counterpart: rather than grade descriptions on a task-agnostic stream, search for the input on which a reading differs from its alternatives, because a description whose only evidence is that nothing yet contradicts it has not been tested. For our predictor that is a design requirement — a worthwhile output names the input where it disagrees with its rivals. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-headvis-index-html, arxiv-2509.13316)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 150): **A component's causal role is a property of its neighbourhood, and the first measured version of that claim in this folder costs one descriptor swap — so downstream context becomes the baseline every read-out of ours has to beat.** The numbers are small and the direction is unmistakable: local descriptors plus one hop of downstream information move the true cause from rank 0.457 to 0.381, while the descriptor the field quotes most — direct logit preference — moves it to 0.446, essentially nothing. That asymmetry supplies the eval shape the folder has been missing for *descriptions*: groups constructed so local descriptors are equal by construction, ground truth held in an intervention, score = position-balanced normalised rank of the true cause. It needs no faithfulness machinery and no human label budget, and it grades the description rather than the circuit — which is exactly the object our predictor emits. The corollary is a downgrade rule: a probe, dictionary entry or node summary that reports only firing examples and top unembeds should be treated as unranked, because those two descriptors were shown here to be near-indistinguishable across features with provably different causal effects. (transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-headvis-index-html, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 150): **The useful output of a mechanistic hypothesis is often a prompt that separates two hypotheses rather than a label, and both case studies here are the same move executed cheaply.** *Green-the-hex-number* versus *green-the-colour-word* became decidable only once the authors built an input where the two readings predict different steering outcomes (the hex-value question), and *describing a willingness to act* versus *acting on it* became decidable only because the audit case had a behaviour that distinguishes them. For a predictive white-box model that is a design requirement more than an evaluation trick: a prediction worth emitting is one that names the input on which it differs from its alternatives, and a description whose only evidence is that nothing so far contradicts it has not been tested. - Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 148): **A causal effect measured on one input is a random variable, and this is the first entry in the folder that puts a number on how random — the base-layer CV of ~0.5 across inputs (and >1 for the gradient approximations) is a floor on the error of every circuit, every feature attribution and every one-input intervention result the folder has recorded.** The decomposition is the part we can import wholesale: intrinsic variance lives in the estimand and cannot be engineered away, estimator variance is the approximations' own contribution and can be reduced, and aggregation-plus-discretisation *amplifies* whatever survives into large structural differences. For a predictive white-box model this reframes the target: the thing worth predicting is not the effect of a component on this input but its population mean over the input--counterfactual distribution, and a predictor that fits single-input effects is fitting the noise term. The practical requirement is that every number our model outputs should come with a resampling error bar computed through the *whole* pipeline, and that a predicted effect smaller than its own error bar be reported as unmeasured rather than as small. It also explains a family of results this folder has logged without understanding them — directions that "survived a rerun" at one seed, circuits whose faithfulness moved with sparsity, effects that flipped under a different ablation — as instantiations of one statistical phenomenon. (arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2611.05033)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 148): **Report the distribution of what your method selects, not only its top-ranked output — and the specific instrument here is a selection-frequency histogram that needs no ground truth.** Across 330 circuits built from gpt2-small's 32,491 edges, only 464 are ever selected, 231 clear 10% frequency, 94 clear 30%, and 7 clear 80%: a stable core under a large noise periphery, obtained for the cost of re-running a pipeline that already exists. This is a cheap, general substitute for the ground-truth circuits this folder keeps saying it lacks, and it applies to every read-out we build — which units a dictionary, probe, attribution or circuit keeps coming back to under resampling is a direct estimate of the explainable-with-confidence part, and the periphery is where every "faithful but fragile" headline lives. Two companion reporting rules come with it and both contradict common practice: report mean **and** coefficient of variation together (the mean of a heavy-tailed Jaccard distribution is misleading alone — 0.561 with CV 0.335 is a bimodal set of circuits, not a mediocre one), and report faithfulness **and** stability as a pair, because they decouple and can even invert the ranking of conditions. (arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2606.16939, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 148): **The counterfactual is part of the question, not a nuisance parameter — and the field's habit of fixing one ablation convention is what makes its findings look like facts about models.** Both of this paper's structural sensitivities point the same way: hyperparameter variants of the same estimator do not converge on a shared circuit but isolate different artefacts of a noisy score distribution (overlap 0.086 and 0.071 in two cases, one edge versus twenty-one at identical error in a third), and sweeping the intervention's noise amplitude moves the identified circuit's reproducibility through a minimum near 0.2 rather than being flat. The consequence for us is a reporting requirement rather than a new method: state the counterfactual distribution as part of the estimand, sweep it rather than picking it, and never compare two circuits — ours or anyone's — without saying which intervention both were computed under. The one genuinely reassuring ordering in the paper is the reverse direction and worth keeping: mechanisms transfer across changes in what inputs *mean* better than across resamples of the same generator (Jaccard 0.790/0.799 versus 0.561), so distribution shift is the easier generalisation test and bootstrap resampling is the one that actually fails — which is the opposite order from how most of this folder evaluates. (arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2602.16698, arxiv-2606.29522)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 147): **A cost metric can manufacture a winner, so any "our units are more compact" claim has to be published on two axes with an exact control — and here the two axes disagree in a way that tells us what the sparsity is for.** On the selected-unit axis the exact SVD and random-orthogonal factorizations are competitive on IOI and at low docstring necessity thresholds, because a unit is a unit regardless of how dense its vectors are; on the active-edge axis SWD wins consistently, because its gain is precisely that each unit touches few input and output coordinates. That distinction is usable for us: a compactness claim about a decomposition is a claim about *connectivity*, not about unit count, and the control that proves it is a reparameterization that reproduces the matrix exactly (SVD gives CE delta 1.6e-6, the 10-seed random-orthogonal control ranges −2.5e-6 to 3.4e-6) so no fidelity difference can be blamed — a strictly cheaper and sharper control than the random-init baselines and shuffled-label nulls this folder has been using for the same purpose, because it holds the object fixed and varies only the property under test. (arxiv-2608.03913, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2611.05033)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 147): **Additivity is a per-site property, not a model property — and this paper gives the two numbers that decide where a surrogate may sum and where it may not.** After the output projection, pair contributions are essentially uncorrelated (95th-percentile absolute correlation 0.0049, 99th 0.0089, one structured tail at 0.345 made of opposed reads with opposed writes cancelling into a positive contribution correlation), so a sum of per-unit effects is a defensible description there; before GELU the same analysis gives moderate, broadly distributed interactions (median ratio 0.089, 99th 0.154, max 0.221, a quarter of pairs at ≥0.10), so a sum is not. The transferable rule for a predictive white-box model is to place non-additivity where the nonlinearity is and to *measure* it as a departure from additivity (a contextual finite difference across the activation, projected through the downstream matrix and normalised by marginal effects) rather than to assume either regime globally — and the framing point is subtler still: low contribution correlation does not mean the units are independent, because a pair with opposed reads and opposed writes can look uncorrelated in isolation and still move the output together. (arxiv-2608.03913, arxiv-2606.16939, arxiv-2602.16698)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 147): **The weights-only floor is the baseline activation-fitted methods owe us, and it is stronger than the field's rhetoric about needing data.** A factorization that uses no calibration data at all — identity Gram, pure weight reconstruction — still produces circuits, at 0.962 held-out docstring sufficiency from three units and 0.986 on greater-than from 256; what calibration buys is behaviour preservation under aggressive sparsification (better CE at the same nonzero budget) while weights-only buys parameter fidelity (0.366 vs 0.415 relative Frobenius error). That is the cleanest two-denominator result in the folder: *which* thing a decomposition preserves is a choice with a measurable trade, and it is the same shape as the reconstruction-error-versus-firing-coverage split the SAE post demanded. For us it sets a mandatory control — any dictionary, transcoder or surrogate trained on activations must be scored against the same factorization computed from weights alone, on the same held-out circuits, because otherwise the gain may be a calibration-distribution artefact rather than structure the model has — and it also gifts a zero-cost instrument for training-trajectory work, since a weights-only factorization can be recomputed at every checkpoint with no activation collection at all. (arxiv-2608.03913, goodfire-com-blog-a-practical-guide-to-saes, arxiv-2602.16698)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 146): **Recurrence turns the depth axis into a grid, and every depth-based claim in this folder silently assumes the grid is one-dimensional — so a looped model is where our vocabulary has to be checked, not just extended.** The structural result is one line (weight tying plus bounded pre-attention states makes the state-to-attention map Lipschitz in the QK product, so a converging loop must give constant attention patterns across passes), and its consequence for us is blunt: in a model whose middle stages repeat inside the block, "layer 18 writes feature F" is not a statement about effective computation, because the same weights are being asked to play several stage roles in sequence. The measurement template worth importing is the (layer × recurrence) grid applied to whatever read-out we use — attribution, probe, ablation effect — because collapsing that grid to depth is exactly the move that would turn a stable cycle into a fake feedforward profile. It also supplies a weight-only diagnostic no forward pass is needed for: the Lipschitz product of the block says, before any experiment, whether the loop is a contraction and therefore whether a predictor trained at one recurrence count may be extrapolated to another. (arxiv-2604.11791, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2602.16698)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 146): **A structural pattern that survives random initialisation cannot be evidence that a task was learned — and here that null argument is decisive rather than decorative, because the phenomenon under study is the architecture's own limiting behaviour.** The per-layer fixed points appear in untrained 12-layer models whenever input injection is present, which converts "trained loops settle into a cycle" from a fact about learning into a fact about the map; and the one untrained configuration that converges without injection converges *degenerately* (every layer to the same state), which is the sharper lesson — a null result on a structural statistic can be an artefact of the null input, so the control has to be checked for the property under test, not merely run. Read against the folder's other untrained-weight controls (a linear map between layers scoring 0.95–0.99 by construction; a Gini concentration already present at zero RL), the general form is now well attested: the cheapest way to falsify a mechanism claim is to run the instrument on a network where the mechanism cannot exist, and the second cheapest is to confirm that the *instrument* still fires on the control where it should. (arxiv-2604.11791, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2610.17093)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 146): **One borrowed statistic decides one story, and this paper is its cleanest demonstration yet: the same models "mirror feedforward stages" under ColSum concentration and do not under residual entropy.** ColSum concentration was built to detect attention sinks; it says Ouro reproduces Llama's mixing stages, and the residual-entropy metric on the identical runs says Ouro departs from feedforward behaviour — with the divergence plausibly explained by the very norm placement that the other metric is insensitive to. The transferable rule is to report the *disagreement between metrics* as a result rather than picking the one that supports the narrative, and to name what each metric is a proxy for before it is used as a verdict. That is the same failure shape the folder has logged repeatedly (a band z-score borrowed across recipes; an effect size compared to a copy effect measured elsewhere; a circuit faithfulness score that moves with sparsity), and it is the reason a stage claim without a stated decision rule — as here, where no threshold separates "has stages" from "does not" — is a reading of a picture rather than a measurement. (arxiv-2604.11791, arxiv-2610.17093, arxiv-2611.05033)

- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 145): **A direction is recovered up to an equivalence class, and the class is measurable before any intervention runs — so "our vector works" and "our vector is the mechanism" are separated by an SVD, not by another steering demo.** The formal content is one line (anything in the Jacobian's null space changes no output, to first order), and the practical content is that the null-space fraction here is 0.86–0.94 of the ambient width, i.e. the unobservable dimensions dominate the geometry of the space our predictors and probes live in. This converts a rhetorical debate into a per-site measurement we can run today: effective rank and null fraction of the activation covariance at every layer we touch, reported next to every read-out accuracy. It also fixes the denominator the folder keeps hand-waving — a probe that recovers 0.8 of something is recovering 0.8 of at most `rank` observable dimensions, and a predictor's ceiling is set by that rank, not by the behaviour's complexity. The corollary for our own write-ups is that a direction should be published as (vector, contrast set, equivalence class dimension), which is exactly the (z, c, π) triple 2602.16698 asked for, arrived at from the measurement side rather than the causal-inference side. (arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2602.16698, arxiv-2611.05033)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 145): **An equivalence test is only as strong as the threshold and the control it is scored against, and this paper's own spread shows how much a conventional cut is doing.** The headline "all ten cells are equivalent" rests on |d| < 0.2, a psychology convention for negligible group differences, applied without an equivalence procedure; the per-cell means run 0.059–0.186 and the null-spanning table reaches 0.243–0.291, so a stricter cut or a proper TOST would make several cells undetermined rather than equivalent. That is not a reason to discard the result — the logit-space ratio R = 0.47–0.73 is threshold-free and points the same way — it is a reason to prefer *paired* statistics with an explicit null over one-sided "below a convention" claims, which is the same lesson the folder already carries from 2610.17093 (a band z-score is a scale, not a p-value) and from 2609.13316 (parallel vs serial dispatch moves a method's score by 0.11). The transferable protocol for us: for every "X does not matter" claim, publish the effect size, the equivalence bound, and a matched perturbation that *should* move the number (here, a norm-matched random direction), because without the last one a null is indistinguishable from an insensitive assay — and this paper has no positive control showing the assay can detect a privileged direction at all. (arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2610.17093, arxiv-2509.13316)

- **A cheap skeleton is a hypothesis generator, and the evidence that raises its status is one intervention per selected edge — not a faithfulness plot**: CircuitLasso recovers a dependency graph over SAE features by regressing each layer on the one before it with Lasso, so nothing is ever intervened on and every edge is a coefficient from correlated activations; its own faithfulness/completeness panels and a novel edge-ablation test are the only places an intervention enters, and they are reported qualitatively. The transferable discipline is to state the object as an estimate with a named residual (they call theirs linearisation error, and refuse causal-sufficiency and independent-noise assumptions outright instead of invoking identifiability theorems they cannot satisfy), then to spend the intervention budget on the few edges the sparsity filter kept rather than on the whole graph. Edge ablation — zero a coefficient in the surrogate and ask whether the prediction moves — is the smallest such test and belongs in our eval set next to node ablation. (arxiv-2606.16939, arxiv-2602.16698, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html)
- **When the ordering is known, fitting to a fixed triangular mask is the whole trick — and it is the one constraint a predictive model of ours is allowed to assume**: the method's scalability is not statistical (a linear surrogate is crude) but structural: the forward pass fixes which component can influence which, so the DAG search collapses to per-layer-pair Lasso with the illegal triangle masked out, and the acyclicity claim becomes a property of the architecture rather than an identifiability argument. For us this is the cleanest available template for "how much of the model may we assume and how much must we estimate", provided we say afterwards which edges are untested. The obvious trap is also shown: once ordering is imposed by fiat, paths that are anti-causal by any human reading (hunger before eating, inverted) come out as edges, and the authors have no test that separates an unusual real dependency from a spurious one. (arxiv-2606.16939, arxiv-2602.16698, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-may-update-index-html)

- **Ground truth first, then intervention — a behaviour edit is only interpretable against a setting where both answers were known in advance**: the evaluation-awareness organism makes the point sharply, because with a model whose deployment behaviour was installed as a known fact, steering toward deployment drives the measured behaviour *below* the model's own deployed rate (under 11% in evaluation contexts against 33–34% deployed), which is a claim no verbalisation metric could have made or refuted. Two cheaper habits come with it and cost almost nothing: run the identical intervention on the pre-fine-tuning checkpoint to show the direction acts on what training touched rather than on outputs generically, and use the exact prompts the vector was built from as a prompt-only baseline, since a mean difference over sentence pairs may be a compressed prompt rather than a state. (arxiv-2510.20487, arxiv-2609.34056, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-cheap-monitors)
- **When the field's success metric is a sentence the model says, the honest next experiment is the one measured off the text channel**: this paper's own conclusion is that suppression of the verbalisation cannot be distinguished from a change in belief, and it points at an activation oracle to settle it — which is exactly the portfolio our project is, so we should read the evaluation-awareness and oracle literature as one thread and treat "the model stops saying X" as a measurement flaw rather than a finding. The 2026-01 addendum is the second lesson in the same direction: a benchmark presented as unbeatable by prompting should be re-attacked after publication, because declarative phrasings later dropped the behaviour to 34–37% and the authors had to narrow their claim. (arxiv-2510.20487, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, arxiv-2609.34056)

- **The right layer-level profile is a pair, not a scalar — (identity share, update linearity) — because one number here is provably blind to whether anything was learned**: this paper's headline is a control, not a result: fitting a linear map between consecutive residual-stream states gives a held-out R² of 0.977–0.984 on two trained decoders, and **randomly initialised** models reproduce 0.95–0.99 on the identical procedure, because the residual passes through untouched and a near-identity map scores well whatever the block computed. Re-targeting the fit at the update (the difference a layer writes) drops mid-stack linearity to 0.35–0.53 and reveals a learned U across six models from three architecture families — large near-linear basis changes at the stack boundaries (LLaMA's layer 1 is 99.6% linearly predictable while its identity baseline captures almost none of its output), small nonlinear refinements in the interior. Two habits follow directly: any linear-read-out claim of ours reports the identity baseline, the update-target statistic, and a random-init control, or it is unfalsifiable; and our per-component profiles should report the pair, since "passes through" and "writes" are nearly complementary axes and either alone is misleading. The pair also predicts behaviour, which is the part that makes it a model: Δ-R² correlates with the realised benefit of substituting a fitted affine map at Spearman ρ = 0.65 across 44 layers, and the predicted failure modes really do fail (the one layer a single map cannot rescue is rescued by four maps routed by k-means, and forcing a patch on a skip-branch window does worse than omitting the layer). (blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, arxiv-2602.16698, transformer-circuits-pub-2024-features-as-classifiers-index-html)
- **Report the controls that a null on your statistic would be, before the statistic, at every scale of this survey**: this entry gives the layer-scale version of the same lesson the folder keeps meeting at other scales — a band z-score whose null is borrowed from another recipe, a Gini concentration that is already in the base model, an L0 pinned by construction, a decoded quantity that the visible context already supplies — and the family resemblance is exact: each is a measurement that cannot fail, and each was caught by running the instrument on an input where the answer was known in advance (untrained weights, zero-RL base, shuffled labels, context-only baseline). The transferable protocol is to name, for every statistic we publish, the *known-negative input* it should give zero on, and to run it; a statistic without such an input is a description, not a test. (blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair, anthropic-com-research-persona-selection-model, arxiv-2610.17093)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 153): **A read-out channel has to be scored on whether the model *had* to use it, and this folder has never separated necessity from propensity for the text channel — the distinction here is the cheapest available partition of every "the trace tells us X" claim.** In an autoregressive Transformer information crosses token boundaries only through generated text, so a hard task forces intermediate state to be written down; on such a task legibility is protected by the architecture rather than by the model's disposition, and it therefore survives training pressure that shrinks or tidies traces. On an easy task the same monitoring result is licensed only by a tendency, and the enumerated fragility mechanisms are precisely the pressures that can override a tendency: outcome-based RL past the point where human text is the optimisation pressure, direct process supervision, indirect pressure through weights shared between trace and answer generation, and monitors whose fixes become selection pressure across runs. The protocol for us is one ablation per claim — remove or corrupt the trace and see whether the capability survives — reported next to the monitoring rate, because the two answers support different words ("the computation lives here" versus "the model usually narrates"). It is the text-channel twin of the folder's probe discipline: neither channel is allowed to claim more than the ablation licenses, and the honest ceiling for both is stated rather than implied. (arxiv-2507.11473, arxiv-2607.03502, arxiv-2603.01437)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 153): **Two measurement channels for one computation can be cross-validated against each other, and the agreement rate is an instrument we can build today — the agenda names exactly the bridge our project needs.** The proposal is to take the tokens a text monitor treats as important and ask whether a white-box method finds the same ones important; divergence is a verdict on at least one of the two instruments, and convergence is the only cheap evidence that the trace and the residual stream are describing the same process rather than two unrelated narratives. This is the constructive version of the folder's repeated finding that CoT usefulness and activation-side read-out strength anticorrelate by task: where both channels fire on the same tokens there is something for a predictive model to be right about, and where only one does, the two entries should be reported as disagreeing rather than averaged into a single "interpretability works" score. The paired instrument is trace perturbation (edit the trace, see if the answer moves), which is activation patching moved to the text channel and inherits its requirement — an intervention plane, a dose, and a stated saturation point. (arxiv-2507.11473, arxiv-2603.01437, goodfire-com-research-reasoning-theater)
- Pattern 2026-11-14 (run 153): **A monitor's false-positive rate is not a verdict, and an evaluation without an adaptive adversary measures a cooperative regime — both stated plainly here and both violated by most of the probe entries in this folder.** Whether a noisy flag is usable depends on what the flag costs to act on: when a flagged response can be resampled cheaply, a high false-positive rate is affordable, so accuracy alone cannot rank two monitors; and a monitor scored against a model that is not trying to evade it is being measured on the easy half of its distribution. The transferable reporting triplet for any classifier or probe we publish is therefore (operating point, cost of acting on a flag, adversary), and the third element is the one nobody reports — the folder's sleeper-agent probes, guardrail classifiers and constitutional classifiers all publish benign-regime scores. This also connects to the folder's standing known-negative rule: the adversary *is* the known-negative input for a monitor, because a monitor that cannot be pushed off its operating point by an adversary has not been shown to be robust, only insensitive. (arxiv-2507.11473, alignment-anthropic-com-2025-cheap-monitors, arxiv-2601.04603)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 155): **A read-out that is scored on a pooled distribution is being graded on the half of the data the model already got right, and this entry is the cleanest arithmetic proof in the folder — 99.5% agreement on IOI's correct prompts alongside 15.2% on its errors, from the published manual circuit, with a normalised faithfulness of 0.956 sitting on top.** The structural point is that these two strata are not two views of one number; a circuit that emits the *task-correct* answer where the model is wrong is a disagreement with the model, not a bonus, so the metric has to condition on the model's own choice and require the identical wrong answer. For us the transfer is immediate and cheap: every probe accuracy, every dictionary-reconstruction score, every surrogate simulation score in this folder is pooled, and the cost of splitting it is one extra groupby. The companion statistic B_err (share of error prompts where the circuit is wrong at all, versus wrong-in-the-same-way) is worth importing too, because it separates "the surrogate knows this input is hard" from "the surrogate predicts this particular mistake" — two very different claims that a single agreement number merges. (arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2510.00845, transformer-circuits-pub-2023-ioi-index-html)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 155): **Exposure to failures is not explanation of failures, and the control that settles it is a one-parameter model — the error-conditioned replacement values here improved error agreement no better than a plain scalar shift toward the wrong name, which is this folder's recurring "did the mechanism do any work?" test in its cheapest form.** Read against the seven remedies they tried, the ordering is instructive: everything that changed the *discovery data* (more errors, upweighted errors, error-enriched sets) bought error reproduction by spending 7–8 points of correct agreement, and nothing closed the gap, whereas the one intervention that changed the *circuit's membership* moved it from 14% to 75% at half a point of cost. That asymmetry is a usable prior for our own surrogate work: when a predictor underperforms on a stratum, the first hypothesis should be that the stratum requires computation the object does not contain, not that the fitting procedure underweighted it — and the test for that is whether adding the missing component helps while a free scalar nudge does not. (arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2611.05033, arxiv-2608.03913)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 155): **Concentration is the evidence that a recovered effect is a mechanism rather than a per-example patch, and here it is one path-patching number: the same inhibition contribution reproduces 120 of 137 newly recovered errors, while the second route reproduces 35 and reproduces none when the intervention is moved to the subject positions.** That triple is a template we can run on any predictive claim of ours — an effect that recurs across examples through a named site, an effect that is real but minority, and an effect that vanishes when the plane of the intervention is shifted one position — and it is a strictly stronger statement than a mean improvement, because it says which examples and through where. It also connects to the folder's standing requirement that an intervention publish its plane: here the plane is literally what distinguishes the working route from the null one, and the same ablation rule is held fixed while only the patch location changes. (arxiv-2609.35686, arxiv-2603.01437, arxiv-2605.10664)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 165): **An explanation of a unit has two ways to be wrong, and this folder has been grading only one of them — recovery catches an account that fails to cover the unit's real effect, and the *inverse* arm catches an account that covers everything and explains nothing; the score that works is the minimum of the pair, not the average.** Here recovery alone is the maximised quantity and it is trivially defeated: the predicate that fires everywhere reaches recovery 1 while saying nothing, which is exactly the shape of the degenerate readers this folder keeps finding — a localisation that does not beat the same number of random components, a linear map that a randomly initialised model also fits, a pooled agreement rate computed where the model was already right. The inverse arm is the cheap fix, and it is a strictly stronger control than the shuffled-label and random-direction nulls because it is computed from the same intervention on the same corpus and differs only in *which positions are restored*. For a predictive white-box model the transfer is direct and nearly free: publish recovery and inverse for every claim that names where a computation happens, plus an explicit coverage number, because a prediction that fires on 90% of inputs cannot be distinguished from one that fires on all of them. (arxiv-2607.02964, arxiv-2605.01555, arxiv-2606.06267)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 165): **The rate you publish should be the rate at the strictest rung you ran, because each rung of held-out discipline knocks out more than half of the previous one and the largest knocks are not uniform — they are concentrated exactly on the model you were using as a baseline.** In-sample → held-out → ten-slice resampled goes 37.3/35.3/15.0, 21.4/17.2/9.6 and 13.2/9.0/1.5, i.e. the dense twin loses 89% of its apparent interpretability while the sparse model loses 60%, so the *comparison* survives only because the fragile side is the one that collapses — report the in-sample number alone and the dense model looks nearly a third as interpretable as the sparse one. The mechanism is worth carrying: the random-chance score under this metric equals the predicate's firing coverage, so an over-fitted predicate on a dense weight sits near chance and regresses *toward* it off-corpus, which means held-out scoring is not a neutral estimator but a monotone amplifier of the true difference. Two habits follow for us: quote the strictest rung, and score every read-out against a chance value that can be computed in closed form before running it, so "is 0.75 good?" has an answer that does not depend on the corpus. (arxiv-2607.02964, arxiv-2510.00845, arxiv-2607.02964)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 165): **A description's language sets its own ceiling, and here the ceiling is demonstrably a property of the grammar rather than of the network — the same string-closing weight scores −0.98 when predicates may look only at the focus token and +0.83 once eight tokens of look-back are allowed, because whether a quote mark opens or closes a string is undecidable from the token.** That is the sharpest available estimate of how much of a "not interpretable" verdict is instrument-limited, and it reframes the folder's description-side results: a missing qualifier in a component description (the headvis lesson) and a predicate language that cannot express the qualifier are the same failure, and only the second is invisible to a human reader of the description. Two operational consequences: when a unit resists explanation, first widen the grammar and re-score before recording a negative, and report the grammar alongside the rate — an interpretability percentage without its predicate language is not comparable across papers. It also explains the residual in this paper's own headline: the weight-level decomposition of the speech-verb neuron recovers five roles that add and cancel into one activation-level label, so the activation summary is a residue of the arithmetic, not a summary of the computation. (arxiv-2607.02964, transformer-circuits-pub-2026-headvis-index-html, arxiv-2605.01555)

- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 156): **Structure is not evidence of function, and this folder has been letting the two stand in for each other in every circuit entry it holds — the fix is one cheap number rather than a new method.** Circuit discovery is a greedy search through a space of individually dispensable edges, so it returns a *sample* from an equivalence class of subgraphs that compute the same thing; small changes in input statistics tip the sampling differently, and the resulting structural difference looks exactly like specialization until it is scored. The transfer-efficiency statistic here is the instrument to copy: take the components a condition nominally owns, graft them onto the shared core, and divide the mean boost they give other conditions by the boost they give their own. A number near one says the "specific" components are generic boosters; the observed 81.4–97.0% across five scales, against 1–3% for random edges of the same count, leaves no room for a specialization reading. Read against the direction-side non-identifiability result, the two entries now say the same thing in two vocabularies — a vector is recovered only up to a Jacobian null space, an edge set only up to a functional equivalence class — so the object a predictive white-box model should be asked to get right is the behavioural contract, not the canonical artifact. (arxiv-2606.06267, arxiv-2602.06801, arxiv-2511.01033)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 156): **Evaluation granularity is a hidden free parameter of every faithfulness score, and here it is worth up to 0.85 accuracy points — larger exactly where the claim matters most.** Source-level evaluation keeps all outgoing edges from any node that contributed at least one circuit edge, which lets unselected pathways carry the computation; edge-level keeps only the discovered edges. The gap grows with model scale (0.22 at 70M to 0.85 at 1.4B), so a scaled-up comparison looks *more* faithful precisely when its edge sets are least stable — a confound that anti-correlates with the quantity being claimed. This is the folder's recurring shape of defect (a band z-score borrowed across recipes, a linear-map R² that a random-init model also achieves, a pooled agreement rate computed over the prompts the model already gets right) arriving at a third scale: a metric that cannot fail. The two habits that transfer immediately: report the *stricter* granularity as primary and treat the looser one as an upper bound, and state for every reported score which set of pathways was allowed to remain live. (arxiv-2606.06267, arxiv-2609.35686, blackboxnlp-2026-linear-layer-repair)
- Pattern 2026-11-15 (run 156): **An effect that survives one ablation rule and vanishes under another was never computation — and two-rule reporting is the cheapest audit we can add to every intervention we publish.** The residual same-band advantage here is significant under resample ablation (p<0.03, d=0.22–0.71), flat across scales, and gone under zero ablation (d≤0.18, and three of five models at exactly nought), which attributes it to the corruption procedure rather than to band-specific circuitry. That is the same lesson the folder drew from patching-plane effects, from KV-cache compounding, and from the source-level inflation above, now stated in its most testable form: hold the contrast and the statistic fixed, change only the ablation rule, and see which of the two moves. The companion finding is that structural instability needs no functional explanation to be harmless — only 21–27% of the largest model's edges appear in all three same-band draws while cross-draw transfer runs 0.990–1.017 — so a single extraction's edge set is a minority of essential edges plus a large inert remainder, and the honest reporting unit is a distribution over extractions with majority-vote aggregation, not a point estimate. (arxiv-2606.06267, arxiv-2604.11791, arxiv-2608.03913)
